faqAnswers.q1: Do I need a subwoofer for a DJ setup?
faqAnswers.a1: Not always required, but highly recommended. A subwoofer adds depth and impact, especially for electronic music and bass-heavy genres.
faqAnswers.q2: How do I connect a subwoofer to my PA system?
faqAnswers.a2: Connect via XLR or RCA cables from your mixer's subwoofer output. Most modern mixers have dedicated sub outputs.

faqAnswers.q1: What is a stage monitor used for?
faqAnswers.a1: Stage monitors let performers hear themselves on stage. They're angled toward the performer and connected to a separate monitor mix from the main PA.
faqAnswers.q2: Can I use a stage monitor as a main speaker?
faqAnswers.a2: Technically yes, but not recommended. Stage monitors are optimized for close-range listening; main PA speakers are designed for audience coverage.

faqAnswers.q1: What height should I set my speaker stands?
faqAnswers.a1: Typically ear-level when seated (4–6 feet high). Adjust based on venue layout and audience positioning.
faqAnswers.q2: Do I need isolation pads under my speakers?
faqAnswers.a2: Yes, isolation pads reduce vibration transfer to the stand and floor, improving sound clarity and preventing feedback.

products.description: Shielded XLR cable with gold-plated connectors and durable PVC jacket.
products.useCase: Audio signal transmission, PA systems, studios
products.bestFor: Any audio setup requiring reliable signal transmission

faqAnswers.q1: What cable length do I need for my PA system?
faqAnswers.a1: Use the shortest cable that reaches your equipment. Longer cables can introduce noise. The ProGrade 25ft is ideal for most small to medium venues.
faqAnswers.q2: What is the difference between XLR and 1/4" cables?
faqAnswers.a2: XLR is balanced and preferred for long runs and professional audio. 1/4" TS is unbalanced and suitable for shorter runs. 1/4" TRS is balanced and a middle ground.
